reason: Start building the heart by combining its muscle with the supporting framework.
expectation: I expect the muscle sheets to attach to the framework as an early heart structure, though other parts will still be needed.

alternatives.reason: The pulmonary vessels also need connecting, but I want to start with the heart.

effect: The heart framework is built, with lining, septa and valves still to fit; its thicker left wall serves the higher-pressure body circuit.
reaction: The contrast between the two ventricular walls makes their different jobs clear.
reason: Add the lining to the open chamber interiors before fitting the remaining parts.
expectation: I expect the chambers to gain a smooth inner lining, while the septa and valves remain to be added.

alternatives.reason: The septa are also needed to divide the heart, but I chose to line it first.

effect: The chamber lining is fitted; the septa and valves remain.
reaction: The fitting was straightforward, with no further detail.
reason: Add the septa to separate the right and left sides of the heart.
expectation: I expect partitions to divide the chambers, leaving the valves to be fitted.

alternatives.reason: The valves are also needed, but I chose to divide the chambers first.

effect: The septa are fitted, leaving the heart valves to add.
reaction: Another straightforward fitting, without further explanation.
reason: Fit the valves to complete the heart's listed components.
expectation: I expect valves to be fitted at the chamber and artery openings; the vessel routes will still need connecting.

alternatives.reason: The pulmonary route also needs building, but I want to finish fitting the heart first.

effect: The heart now has its lining, septa and valves fitted; both vessel routes still need connecting.
reaction: The valve fitting was straightforward, though it did not yet show how the valves work.
reason: Build the pulmonary route so it can eventually connect the heart to the lung circuit.
expectation: I expect the pulmonary capillaries to connect the artery and vein trees into a lung vessel network.

alternatives.reason: Connecting the systemic network is also needed, but I chose to prepare the pulmonary route first.

effect: The pulmonary arteries, capillaries and veins now form a connected route ready to join the heart.
reaction: The connection is clear, though the result adds little detail about lung exchange.
reason: Connect the pulmonary route to the heart now that it is assembled.
expectation: I expect the pulmonary vessels to join the heart's right and left sides, with the systemic route still to add.

alternatives.reason: The systemic network also needs connecting, but I chose to attach the newly built pulmonary route first.

effect: The pulmonary loop is connected, leaving the systemic openings free.
reaction: The remaining openings make the next connection clear.
reason: Connect the systemic network to the heart; it is the only offered combination.
expectation: I expect the systemic vessels to join the heart, completing the two vessel routes; blood may still need to be added.
